sense: shall I …? asking what to do

terms.gloss: what shall I do? what am I to do?
terms.grammar: the present subjunctive in a question, negative nōn; of the past, the imperfect subjunctive
evidence: Ter. Eun. 46: Quid igitur faciam? nōn eam?
Ter. Eun. 49: Redeam? nōn, sī mē obsecret.
terms.comment: Asking oneself or another what to do puts the verb in the subjunctive. Of the past: Quid facerem?, what was I to do? (Ter. Eun. 831).

terms.gloss: shall I …? do you want me to …? (offering)
evidence: Plaut. Stich. 486: vīn' ad tē ad cēnam veniam?
terms.comment: The offer of comedy; see want for volō with the subjunctive.

phrases.english: So what shall I do? Not go?

phrases.latin: Exclūsit: revocat. Redeam? nōn, sī mē obsecret.
phrases.english: She shut me out; now she calls me back. Shall I go back? No, not if she begs me.

phrases.latin: vīn' ad tē ad cēnam veniam? — Sī possim, velim.
phrases.english: Shall I come to dinner at your house? — I’d like that, if I could manage it.
“How far shall I get?” you ask. As far as you try.

phrases.latin: Tua culpa. — Quid agerem? — Adulēscentī mōrem gestum oportuit.
phrases.english: Your fault. — What was I to do? — You should have humoured the young man.

sources: Lewis & Short: facio · Lewis & Short: volo
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae), checked against the editions named there.

Terence and Plautus checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026): the Eunuchus in the Oxford numbering, which runs one line ahead of Parry’s in that play from about line 390 (so Parry’s 830 is line 831); Terence is spelled as in the loci collections (adulēscentī for Parry’s adolescenti).
